solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Medic becoming enmeshed in sex scandal

indicators.note: being enmeshed means twined through one another, so the two short pieces are woven together letter by letter

parts.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor
IT is crossword shorthand for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A doctor gets caught up in a tabloid sex scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming enmeshed in' means the two pieces are twined letter by letter, alternating, not one placed inside the other; the parse can only show this as a rearrangement. IT is sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt is gossip or damaging information, the stuff a scandal is made of.

clue.text: Drops Arab leader of alarming intemperance

parts.note: to drop is to dip
an Omani is an Arab from Oman

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of alarming

explanation.surface: An Arab chief falls into worrying heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipsomania is a craving for alcohol, the extreme of intemperance or excess in drinking.

clue.text: Novelist initially failing to get out of bed

indicators.note: the novelist's initial letter fails, so it is taken away

parts.note: Marcel Proust, French novelist

explanation.surface: A novelist who at first can't get himself out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Proust famously wrote much of his novel in bed, which makes the picture apt.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust someone is to rouse them and drive them out, especially from bed.

clue.text: Use different words for average verbal altercations

parts.note: par is the average or normal standard

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the word for altercations is said out loud

parts.note: affrays are public brawls or altercations

explanation.surface: Instructions to reword a description of ordinary verbal quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: AFFRAYS, said aloud, sounds like 'a phrase'.
explanation.definitionFit: To paraphrase is to restate something in other wording.

clue.text: Chap nearer us oddly entering hole-in-the-wall club

indicators.note: entering means going inside the cash-machine letters

parts.note: a hole in the wall is British slang for a cash machine, an ATM
HE stands for a chap, a male

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of nearer us

explanation.surface: A man nearer to us strangely walking into a scruffy little club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hole-in-the-wall' looks like a description of a seedy club but is a British name for a cash machine. The Athenaeum is a famous gentlemen's club on Pall Mall in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenaeum is an example of a London gentlemen's club.

clue.text: Gulf Times probing idiot

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an ass is a fool
times, as in multiplication, is BY (three by four)

explanation.surface: A newspaper, perhaps the Gulf Times, investigating a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulf is a deep chasm, the same as an abyss.

clue.text: According to Spooner, catch sight of the female firebrand

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two pieces exchange their first sounds

parts.note: to spot is to catch sight of
her is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism about spotting a fiery woman.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOT HER becomes HOT SPUR when the SP and H sounds are swapped. Hotspur is Henry Percy, the hot-headed rebel in Shakespeare's Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspur is a rash, impetuous person, much like a firebrand or agitator.

clue.text: Caught out every time, can't con iconic film director

indicators.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught, and every one is taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: A director's every attempt at deception is exposed; his iconic swindles fail.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop all four Cs from CAN'T CON ICONIC to leave ANT ON IONI. Michelangelo Antonioni was the Italian director of Blow-Up and L'Avventura.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo Antonioni is an example of an Italian film director.

clue.text: Genuine cases of economic hindsight

indicators.note: the cases of words are their outside letters, here of economic and hindsight

explanation.surface: Real examples of economic wisdom after the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German borrowing meaning authentic or real.

clue.text: Plant first half of mint and second half of sage

indicators.note: and joins the mint piece to the second-and-sage group that follows it, in that order
the first half of mint is its opening two letters

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second

indicators.note: half of sage here means its front two letters, kept while the rest goes

explanation.surface: A recipe-like instruction blending mint and sage halves to make a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is not 'second half' but MO, a moment; the surface invites reading 'second half of sage' as GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a kind of acacia shrub with fluffy yellow flowers.

clue.text: Rather vulgar dons work with affected modesty

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so one piece wears the other around it

parts.note: to ply is to work at, as in ply a trade
rudish means somewhat rude or vulgar

explanation.surface: Academic dons whose rather coarse work is met primly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers but means puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudishly describes behaving with excessive or affected modesty.

clue.text: Someone short of time heading off from sports field

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, comes off the playing area

parts.note: a pitch is a field for football or cricket

explanation.surface: A player short of time leaving the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Titch is British slang for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: A titch is an informal British word for a small person or child.

clue.text: Tired old couple filling pot

indicators.note: filling means going inside the vessel

parts.note: an urn is a pot or vase
a couple is two

explanation.surface: An exhausted elderly pair filling a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Outworn means worn out or exhausted, so tired.

clue.text: Inclined to drink wine, not whiskey

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: not removes the whiskey letter from wine

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone disposed to drink wine rather than whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' seems to mean willing, but here it means lying back.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on one's back, reclining rather than upright.

clue.text: Riyadh ends riots in waterless compounds

indicators.note: riots suggests letters running wild and rearranged

explanation.surface: Riots in Riyadh come to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Anhydrides are chemical compounds formed by removing water.

clue.text: At random, notice a new kind of film

indicators.note: making a new kind of something means reworking its letters

explanation.surface: A randomly noticed new type of film.
explanation.definitionFit: An animated cartoon is a kind of film made from drawings.

clue.text: Start hesitating hopelessly after husband leaves

indicators.note: hopelessly suggests something in a muddle, so the letters are rearranged
the husband leaving means that letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone dithering hopelessly once her husband walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes H out of HESITATING; 'hopelessly' rearranges the remaining ESITATING.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to start or set something in motion.

clue.text: Swindle corporation and see insulting behaviour

parts.note: a con is a swindle
corporation is old slang for a paunch or belly, a tum
a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city

explanation.surface: Cheating a company and witnessing rude conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Contumely is insolent, scornful treatment or language.

clue.text: Court refused to give orders to intelligence agency

indicators.note: refused means turned away, so the court letters are not admitted

parts.note: to instruct is to give orders
mentality means mental power or intelligence

explanation.surface: A court declined to give instructions to a spy agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence agency' reads as one phrase, a spy service, but it splits: 'intelligence' is wordplay and 'agency' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Instrumentality means the means or agency by which something is done.

clue.text: Dictator's private bitterness

indicators.note: a dictator is one who speaks words out loud for writing, so this is said, not spelt

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, such as a private

explanation.surface: A dictator's private resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant, but it means one who dictates aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep, long-lasting bitterness or resentment.

clue.text: Inanity, initially taken for sharpness

indicators.note: the initial letter is taken away

parts.note: vacuity is emptiness of mind, inanity

explanation.surface: Mistaking stupidity for keen wit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' suggests taking the I of Inanity, but it is the first letter of VACUITY that is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity is sharpness of mind or perception.

clue.text: Singer hiding at football match after retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the score reads backwards

parts.note: a hiding is a thrashing, and a ten-nil scoreline is one at football

explanation.surface: A singer hides out at a football match after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' seems to mean concealment but is a heavy defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small finch known as a songbird.

clue.text: Liking some of Calcutta's temples

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fondness for some of the temples of Calcutta.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste for something is a liking or preference.

clue.text: One wrongly claiming loan shark hides money

indicators.note: hides means keeps tucked inside

parts.note: a usurer lends at extortionate interest
P, a penny, stands for money

explanation.surface: A loan shark stashing cash while making false claims.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper seizes a throne or right they have no claim to.

clue.text: Danger for every single learner

parts.note: per means for each
I is the Roman numeral one
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A hazard faced by every lone learner driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious danger or risk.

clue.text: Following outburst, turned up and spat

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a fit is an outburst

explanation.surface: After an outburst, someone arrived and spat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spat' looks like a verb but is a noun, a petty quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff and a spat are both minor quarrels.

clue.text: Unlimited time in the past for last phase of cricket?

indicators.note: unlimited means without its limits, the outside letters

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Endless time spent in the closing stage of a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket is the insect, not the game: the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, adult stage of an insect such as a cricket.

clue.text: Protected her eldest, snarling

indicators.note: snarling as in tangled up, so the letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A mother shielded her eldest child, growling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltered means shielded or protected from harm.

clue.text: Symbol of French monarchy surely fled after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: French royalty surely fled after the Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleur-de-lys, a stylised lily, was the emblem of the French kings.

clue.text: Regularly applauds sign of positivity

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of applauds

explanation.surface: Steady applause as a sign of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The plus sign marks a positive number or quantity.
